subject: Model bundle publishing onboarding & revenue share negotiation
messages:
From: Kate Miller <kate@opencorelabs.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal - OpenCore <legal@opencorelabs.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model weights distribution & potential partnership

Hi Ava & Camila,

Thanks for taking the time last week. OpenCore Labs is ready to move forward with distributing our 3-model bundle (OC-Base, OC-Large, OC-Instruction) and we wanted to share a starter package to get technical and commercial talks rolling. Attached: OpenCore_Weights_Release_NDA.pdf and a draft term sheet (revshare-term-sheet-v1.xlsx).

High-level asks from our side:
- Non-exclusive distribution across marketplaces and partner catalogs
- A coordinated embargo/canary release (2-week window) before public mirrors
- Revenue share + reporting cadence (monthly)
- Technical validation checklist: checksums, model card, quantization guidance, and a staging S3 with time-limited credentials

Two quick questions for Redwood:
1) Do you accept publisher-provided S3 staging for initial validation (we can rotate creds and provide presigned URLs)?
2) Does Redwood require a minimum revshare floor or prefer a fixed fee for on-prem customers?

We'd love to schedule a 30-min session to align on the onboarding checklist and legal redlines — Camila, would next Tue or Wed morning PT work?

Attaching the NDA and term sheet for review.

Best,
Kate Miller
Head of Partnerships | OpenCore Labs
kate@opencorelabs.ai

Attachments: OpenCore_Weights_Release_NDA.pdf, revshare-term-sheet-v1.xlsx

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Miller <kate@opencorelabs.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model weights distribution & potential partnership

Hi Kate — thanks, and great to see this moving quickly. Looping in our partnerships and legal ops.

Quick answers up front:
- Yes, we can validate from a publisher-provided S3 staging bucket for an initial canary, provided you supply presigned URLs and a checksum manifest (SHA256).
- Redwood prefers revshare for marketplace distribution; we typically propose a 60/40 split (publisher/platform) for non-exclusive bundles, but are open to a different gross-split or a hybrid fixed + revshare for enterprise on-prem deals.

Please see the onboarding checklist below (short form) — we'll share a formal doc in Drive after sign-off: 
- Signed NDA (received) and POA from legal
- Model artifacts: weights (.pth/.safetensors), tokenizer files, model card, LICENSE.txt
- Checksum manifest (SHA256) for each artifact
- Intended quantization guidance & any optimizations that change behavior
- Embargo/canary dates and allowed mirror list
- Billing & revshare contact and reporting email
- Security questionnaire (if red flags arise we may request SOC2 evidence)

Camila — would you like to take lead on commercial redlines? Sergio and Marcus, can you confirm the runtime validation steps and whether our Dedicated customers need additional licensing terms?

Kate — we can do Tue 2027-04-06 10:00 PT or Wed 2027-04-07 09:00 PT — pick what works and we'll send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Partner Solutions | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai

From: Kate Miller <kate@opencorelabs.ai>

Cc: Legal - OpenCore <legal@opencorelabs.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model weights distribution & potential partnership

Thanks Ava — taking those in order.

1) S3 staging: yes, we'll provide presigned URLs valid for 72 hours per object; we'll also include a checksum manifest and a small verification script.
2) Revshare: legal has proposed a starting split of 70/30 (publisher/platform) in the attached v1, accounting for our go-to-market support commitments. We're open to negotiation; the key for us is predictable reporting and a fair baseline for our team.
3) Embargo: OpenCore is comfortable with a 2-week canary before broad redistribution; we'd like all mirrors to be notified and given a mirror whitelist.

I'll attach the revshare-term-sheet-v1.xlsx again and ask Legal to highlight IP/export-control sections. They are OK with non-exclusive terms but want clarity around who can host quantized artifacts and redistribution to third-party mirrors.

Camila — does Redwood require a specific audit log format for revenue reports? If yes, we can align on a template before signing.

We can take Tue 04-06 10:00 PT. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Kate

Attachments: revshare-term-sheet-v1.xlsx

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Miller <camila@opencorelabs.ai>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model bundle publishing onboarding & revenue share negotiation

Kate — thanks for the details and for sending the draft. I reviewed the term sheet with Legal and have the following commercial counterpoints: 

- Revshare: Redwood proposes 60/40 (publisher/platform) with standard marketplace reporting and monthly settlements net-30. This aligns with our current publisher cohorts and gives us flexibility on enterprise carve-outs.
- Non-exclusivity: OK, we prefer non-exclusive to keep distribution broad.
- Mirrors: we require a mirror disclosure list; any public mirrors must wait until the end of the canary window and be notified in writing.
- Quantized artifacts: publishers may provide quantized artifacts, but redistribution of publisher-supplied quantized files requires explicit written permission (to avoid drift in behavior).

Operational asks: 
1) Please upload the bundle to the staging S3 (we'll validate checksums and run our suite).
2) Provide a manifest with SHA256 and the tokenizer/test prompts we can run to confirm parity.
3) We'll need an executed NDA + a countersigned DocuSign for the rolling revshare term sheet.

Sergio & Marcus — can you list 3 validation items we must pass before we open the canary? Marcus, please call out any Dedicated/On-prem licensing flags.

Assuming the above, we'll prepare a redline of the term sheet and send via DocuSign by Tue morning so Legal can countersign during the call if needed. Also proposing to add a 30-day rolling performance SLA clause for latency regressions that materially affect customer experiences.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Attachment reference: OpenCore_Weights_Release_NDA.pdf (we received and logged in our system)

From: Kate Miller <kate@opencorelabs.ai>

Camila / Ava — thanks for the counterpoints, all reasonable. Confirming next steps from OpenCore: 

- Accept the 60/40 non-exclusive split. We appreciate the standardized reporting and net-30 cadence.
- We'll upload the artifacts to the staging S3 by Tue 04-06 06:00 PT and include a checksum manifest and a small verification script. S3 staging details and one-time creds are in s3-access-instructions.txt (attached).
- We can agree to the mirror notification requirement and to restrict redistribution of quantized artifacts unless explicitly permitted.
- Legal will sign the NDA and the revshare DocuSign link (please send the PowerForm post-redline).

Technical: below is the presigned manifest excerpt and checksums (full manifest attached in S3 files):
